title: Graphing a Reflected and Vertically Shifted Square Root
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1 - sqrt(x) by identifying its parent function, transformations, domain, range, and intercepts.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \sqrt{x} \text{ reflected across x-axis and shifted up } 1;\quad \text{Domain: } [0, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (-\infty, 1],\quad \text{Intercepts: } (0, 1),\ (1, 0)

steps.title: Decompose the Transformations from y = sqrt(x)
steps.explanation: Start with y = sqrt(x), reflect across the x-axis by multiplying by -1 to get y = -sqrt(x), and then shift upward by 1 unit to get y = 1 - sqrt(x).
steps.why: Negating a function reflects its graph across the x-axis, and adding 1 translates it vertically upward.

steps.title: Find the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The square root is defined for x >= 0. Since -sqrt(x) <= 0 takes all values in (-infinity, 0], adding 1 yields the range (-infinity, 1].
steps.why: Reflecting [0, infinity) to (-infinity, 0] and adding 1 produces the interval (-infinity, 1].

steps.title: Determine the Endpoint and Intercepts
steps.explanation: The graph begins at the y-intercept (0, 1), crosses the x-axis at (1, 0), and continues decreasing into the fourth quadrant through (4, -1) and (9, -2).
steps.why: Setting x = 0 gives y = 1, and solving 1 - sqrt(x) = 0 gives sqrt(x) = 1, or x = 1.
